title: Weekly Deep Dive: Boeing's Impossible Week — Winning Big While Falling Behind
summary: Boeing landed a massive Turkish Airlines order and a $36 billion week, but the 737 MAX 10 still can't get FAA sign-off, and the China mega-deal is slipping away for good. Ryan and Hope dig into why airlines keep buying a jet that isn't even certified yet, how Airbus's own quality crisis is handing Boeing a rare opening, and what losing China really costs Boeing over the next decade.

topic.topic: Boeing's 737 MAX 10 software issues and delivery delays threaten the aircraft's certification timeline amid massive new orders from Turkish Airlines and supply chain pressure from the A321neo backlog.
topic.why: This story appeared in multiple sources this week and represents a critical inflection point for Boeing's recovery. With Turkish Airlines just ordering 150 MAX aircraft and Boeing facing FAA software reviews on the MAX 10, the company is simultaneously winning massive orders while struggling to deliver on existing commitments. The A321neo's quality defects are forcing Airbus to revive dormant factories, creating a rare window where Boeing could gain share—but only if it can clear certification hurdles.
key_facts: FAA is reviewing a software issue that could delay 737 MAX 10 certification further
Turkish Airlines placed order for up to 150 737 MAX aircraft despite Boeing's quality struggles
Boeing's China mega-order (200+ jets) is now in serious jeopardy, possibly abandoned entirely
Airbus A321neo has fuselage coating defects affecting 500+ aircraft, forcing production workarounds
Boeing won a $36 billion order this week but stock fell due to MAX 10 certification concerns
